notes: V-2 (A-4) Model 39: r_t 0.2060 m (A_t 0.13332 m^2) at p0 1.57 MPa with ideal c* 1612 m/s gives delivered mass flow 138.1 kg/s (eta_c* 0.94) and sea-level thrust 270.5 kN (eta_Cf 0.95), against published 125.0 kg/s and 249.0 kN — +10.5% on mass flow, +8.7% on thrust. Published performance figures other than the Redstone throat diameter are commonly-cited values, not measurements this repo verifies; they are a sanity check on the derived geometry, not a reference.

Every historical preset clears the 0.40 Summerfield separation threshold at its own default altitude; the tightest is Titan I LR87-AJ-3 (1 of 2) at p_e/p_a 0.630. The two altitude-optimised presets are asserted in BOTH directions: Atlas LR105-5 (default 25 km) and Titan I LR91-AJ-3 (default 60 km, clamped to the model's 58 km ceiling) must separate at sea level, or their non-zero default would be decoration rather than a fix. Every other preset must NOT separate at 0 km, or it would need a default of its own.

Published performance figures other than the Redstone throat diameter are commonly-cited values, not measurements this repo verifies; they are a sanity check on the derived geometry, not a reference.

Redstone throat area recovered from the rasterized wall: 0.121847 m^2 at 4x the production radial resolution (+0.067% vs the published 0.121766 m^2), 0.122151 m^2 on the production grid (+0.316%). The production figure is biased HIGH by column averaging: a column integrates the wall over its own width and r(z) is quadratic at a throat, so the cell-mean area exceeds the minimum by ~(dz^2/12)/R_arc — with dz = 0.145 r_t and the 0.382 r_t downstream arc that is ~0.45%. It falls as dz^2, which the refined figure confirms. The preset's own r_t gives a geometric area of 0.121798 m^2 (+0.027%).
